thesis: Held position, fresh thesis. Dell reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-09-01: record revenue of $47.0B, up 58% year over year, and record non-GAAP diluted EPS of $7.04, up 203% year over year, both above consensus (adjusted EPS $2.17 above the $4.87 estimate, revenue $2.16B above estimate). Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue rose 89% to $31.8B; the company booked $60.9B of AI server orders in the quarter and exited with a record $95.0B AI backlog, taking trailing-twelve-month AI orders to $131.7B. Dell raised full-year FY27 guidance by $25B to a $192.0B revenue midpoint (~70% growth) and lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to ~$25.50 (~150% growth). The strongest counter-case is that AI server revenue carries structurally thinner margins than Dell's legacy infrastructure mix, so a record backlog need not convert into profit — but even with that mix shift already running through the quarter, non-GAAP EPS grew 203% and Dell raised its own forward EPS guide by roughly the same proportion as revenue, which is the company committing to the conversion rather than deferring it. Verification limit: only the non-GAAP EPS line was confirmed in the sources read this run; the corresponding GAAP EPS was not stated in any source read, so the GAAP profitability print is unconfirmed and is not asserted here. Litigation check: the Dell Class V stockholder litigation was settled for $1B and approved in April 2023; no active matter with a scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days surfaced this run. This suggests the disclosed backlog and raised guidance continue to support holding.
invalidation: A subsequent Dell disclosure showing AI backlog conversion slipping (backlog flat or falling quarter over quarter, or ISG operating margin compressing), or a cut to the FY27 $192B revenue / $25.50 non-GAAP EPS guidance.
sources: BigGo Finance (Dell Q2 FY27 earnings call): https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_DELL_2026-09-01
Labaton Keller Sucharow (In re Dell Technologies Class V Stockholders Litigation): https://www.labaton.com/cases/in-re-dell-technologies-inc-class-v-stockholders-litigation

thesis: Held position, fresh thesis. On 2026-09-02 Microsoft disclosed standalone Azure revenue for the first time and announced a reporting overhaul consolidating its operating divisions from three to two: Azure revenue was $29.4B in the quarter ended 2026-06-30 and $101.9B for the full fiscal year, and commercial remaining performance obligations reached $678B, up 84% year over year. Microsoft Cloud revenue in that quarter was $59.3B, up 27%. The stock closed at $510.12 on 2026-09-03, up 2.68%. The larger part of the 60-day move came earlier, on the fiscal Q4 print reported 2026-07-29, after which guidance of $89.85-$90.95B was given for fiscal Q1 against an LSEG consensus of $89.66B. The strongest counter-case is that a change in disclosure creates no new cash flow — a company that merely starts showing a number it always had should not re-rate on that alone, and Amazon and Google remain direct competitors for the same cloud spend. What answers it is the figure disclosed alongside the format change: $678B of commercial remaining performance obligations, up 84%, is contracted future revenue rather than presentation, and it is that backlog, not the reporting change, that the disclosure made visible. Litigation check: no active lawsuit or regulatory investigation naming Microsoft with a scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days surfaced in this run's research. This suggests the disclosed contracted backlog continues to support holding.
invalidation: A quarterly disclosure showing Azure dollar revenue decelerating materially or commercial remaining performance obligations flat-to-down, or fiscal Q1 revenue landing below the $89.85B low end of the company's own guidance.

thesis: Held position, fresh thesis. Nvidia's own newsroom release for fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 2026-07-26) reports revenue of $96.2B, up 18% sequentially and up 106% year over year, with GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins both at 75.0% — the two bases agree, so there is no adjusted-versus-reported divergence to reconcile here. On 2026-09-03 Nvidia announced the acquisition of Hugging Face. The stock sits 2.8% below its 52-week high and the 60-day move is +17.8%. The strongest counter-case is regulatory: the Commerce Department division that enforces semiconductor export controls is reportedly examining how Chinese AI developers rent Nvidia-powered compute located outside China, which could extend restrictions to a channel that is currently legal. Even with that inquiry open, it is an examination with no scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline disclosed, and the quarter just reported delivered 106% growth at a 75.0% gross margin under the export regime already in force — the restrictions that exist today have not bent either the growth rate or the margin, so an inquiry into an adjacent channel does not by itself change the read. Next earnings are scheduled for 2026-11-19, well beyond this position's next daily review. This suggests the disclosed results continue to support holding.
invalidation: A formal export-control action restricting offshore rental of Nvidia compute by Chinese developers, or a quarter in which data center revenue growth decelerates sharply or gross margin falls materially below the 75% level just reported.

thesis: Held position, fresh thesis; no Step 2 signal fired (60-day move 0.25%, volume 1.09x, 26.4% below the 52-week high), so this is the deterioration check rather than a new setup. Sources read this run report that SanDisk held an investor day on 2026-08-13 setting long-term targets including double-digit revenue growth through 2030 and an 80% non-GAAP gross margin, initiated a $14B stock buyback, and has recent supply agreements carrying a floor price of roughly $0.29 per gigabyte, described as broadly in line with Q2 2026 average selling prices. The stock rose about 8% on 2026-09-04 alongside a 5% gain in Micron, attributed to tight NAND supply driven by AI infrastructure demand. The evidence is genuinely offsetting rather than net-directional. The catalyst is a NAND pricing cycle, which is an industry-wide condition rather than a company-specific disclosure, and the price floor cited is described as in line with — not above — current selling prices, so it caps downside rather than signalling further pricing gains. The counter-case is that NAND is a commodity cycle that has historically reversed hard, and this run cannot settle it: over the full 60-day window the stock is net flat (1744.43 to 1740.00) despite swinging from roughly 1015 to 1787 inside it, which is the market itself failing to reach a verdict after a 525% year-to-date run. Litigation: an active consumer class action over allegedly defective SanDisk drives is before Judge Rita F. Lin in the Northern District of California, but the class-certification hearing dates found were in January 2026 and no scheduled ruling, hearing or deadline in the next ~90 days surfaced, so it is noted but not flagged. Nothing disclosed indicates deterioration, so this still supports holding.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing breaking below the disclosed ~$0.29/GB floor level, a SanDisk disclosure walking back the investor-day margin or growth targets, or suspension of the $14B buyback.
sources: Daily Journal (In re SanDisk SSDs Litigation): https://www.dailyjournal.com/article/389346-judge-signals-doubt-about-nationwide-class-in-sandisk-defective-drive-case

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -31.0%. Rocket Lab reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-11 with record revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year, and a $2.36B backlog, alongside an adjusted loss of $0.08 per share; the stock fell about 8% on the print. The decline is driven by several factors that this run cannot resolve into one dominant cause. Company-specific: Rocket Lab still expects Neutron to reach the launch pad in Q4 2026 but stopped short of reaffirming a launch before year-end, saying the window for an end-of-year launch is narrowing — a disclosed schedule slip on the program the equity story rests on. Sector-wide: the shares peaked at $151 in May and were caught in the rotation out of space names that followed the SpaceX IPO, which is a market-structure move rather than anything Rocket Lab disclosed. Externally: NASA awarded Blue Origin a Mars communications contract worth up to $700M, and there has been attention on recent executive stock sales. The counter-case is real — 62% revenue growth and a record backlog are not the profile of a deteriorating business, and the company had booked over $663M in new government awards heading into the print — but it is not settled, because the Neutron timing that would convert that backlog is exactly what slipped. With a macro rotation, a disclosed schedule slip and a lost contract all contributing and none clearly dominant, this suggests standing aside rather than initiating.
invalidation: A Rocket Lab announcement confirming a firm Neutron first-flight date, or conversely an explicit slip of Neutron out of Q4 2026 into 2027, either of which would resolve the dominant open question.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move +28.7%. Snowflake reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-09-02: revenue $1.55B, up 35% year over year against a $1.48B consensus; product revenue $1.49B, up 37%; non-GAAP operating income $237M versus a $187M estimate; adjusted EPS $0.62 versus $0.45 expected. It raised FY27 product revenue guidance to $6.07B from $5.84B and guided fiscal Q3 product revenue to $1.59B against $1.50B consensus, and lifted its full-year non-GAAP operating margin forecast to 14.5% from 13.5%. Both metrics, as required: on a GAAP basis the same quarter produced an operating loss of $263.0M and a net loss of $191.7M, or $0.55 per share (narrowed from a $297.9M, $0.89 per share loss a year earlier), with $456.4M of stock-based compensation charges accounting for most of the gap between the two bases. The evidence is therefore genuinely mixed rather than net-clean: accelerating product revenue and a raised guide on one side, a still-loss-making GAAP business and — per one account of the print — a remaining-performance-obligation figure that went the other way while almost everything else beat. The counter-case that consumption revenue can decelerate is answered by the acceleration to 37% and the raised Q3 and FY guides; the counter-case about earnings quality is named and not answered. The tape reflects that: shares spiked above $375 after hours on the print and have since given back to $338. This suggests owning it only at a size that assumes the GAAP question stays open.
invalidation: Product revenue growth decelerating below the guided trajectory, the FY27 $6.07B product revenue guide being cut, or GAAP operating loss widening rather than narrowing year over year.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -28.3%. Astera Labs reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-04 with revenue of $392.4M, up 104% year over year, and the shares fell 12% on the print, with sources citing higher operating expenses from continued product-roadmap investment plus persistent concerns about customer concentration and valuation. Operationally the company disclosed that its high-radix Scorpio X-Series entered volume production and that management expects Scorpio to become its largest product family in Q3, one quarter earlier than previously projected. The September leg down came after Morgan Stanley said the Intel-Nvidia agreement to co-develop PC and data center chips would affect Astera Labs' business. That last item is the reason this stays at low conviction: the most recent driver is an analyst read-through about a competitive threat, not anything Astera Labs disclosed, and this run cannot settle whether an Intel-Nvidia interconnect partnership displaces Astera's connectivity content or leaves it intact. The counter-case is named and unresolved. What is disclosed — 104% revenue growth and a flagship product ramping a quarter ahead of plan — remains net supportive, so this reads as ownable at low conviction rather than as a business in decline.
invalidation: An Astera Labs disclosure showing revenue growth decelerating sharply or a named hyperscaler customer reducing content, or confirmation that the Intel-Nvidia collaboration displaces Astera's connectivity silicon in a design win.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -22.7%; the stock is down roughly 54% from a record $133.09 close on 2026-05-28. Unlike most of the decliners screened this run, the driver here is disclosed operational slippage rather than rotation. AST SpaceMobile had guided to 45-60 satellites in orbit by the end of 2026, cut that to 45 after losing BlueBird 7 in orbit in April, then in its Q2 report in July pushed the 45-satellite target to early 2027; sources dated 2026-09-03 report the commercial launch target moving to 2027. Q2 revenue was $31.5M, up from $1.2M a year earlier, but the net loss widened to $230.9M in the quarter, and the constellation is being built largely on borrowed money, which makes the equity directly sensitive to funding costs; cash burn, dilution and insider selling are all cited as pressures. The FCC granted only a temporary 30-day authorization restricted to non-commercial 800 MHz testing, so permanent commercial authority is still outstanding. The counter-case is that US Mobile has said it plans to launch AST-powered direct-to-cell coverage on its Verizon-based Warp network in Q4 — but that plan depends on the same satellites and the same permanent FCC authority that have both slipped, so it does not resolve the schedule question, it restates it. This suggests standing aside.
invalidation: Permanent FCC commercial authorization being granted, or AST reaching the 45-satellite constellation target, either of which would convert the schedule from an open question into a delivered milestone.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move +21.8%; shares up 41.8% in the past month. Two things are established and one is not. Established: in March 2026 the FDA approved Lifyorli (relacorilant) with nab-paclitaxel for adult patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, and Corcept presented Phase 3 ROSELLA overall-survival data at ASCO 2026 showing a 35% reduction in risk of death (HR 0.65; p=0.0004) with median overall survival of 16.0 months versus 11.9 months for nab-paclitaxel alone. That is a completed regulatory approval plus disclosed survival data, and it diversifies revenue beyond Korlym. Not established: the move that triggered this signal rests mainly on Corcept announcing it will resubmit the new drug application for relacorilant in Cushing's syndrome, with the FDA indicating a PDUFA date roughly six months after resubmission. A resubmission is not an approval, and the reason a resubmission is needed at all is that the earlier relacorilant filing in Cushing's was rejected — that counter-case is engaged here and cannot be settled by anything disclosed, since the outcome is a future agency decision. The approved oncology indication and its survival benefit support owning the name; the Cushing's resubmission is optionality with an unresolved regulatory history behind it, which is what holds conviction down.
invalidation: A second complete response letter or refusal-to-file on the resubmitted Cushing's NDA, or Lifyorli launch metrics showing the ovarian cancer indication failing to diversify revenue away from Korlym.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -21.6%; shares fell roughly 28% over 30 days and broke below $90. The pressure is a combination of disclosed financials and unconfirmed reporting, and this run cannot resolve them into a single read. Disclosed: Intel Foundry logged a $2.8B quarterly operating loss and Intel expanded its 2026 capital expenditure plan to over $20B to fund the foundry turnaround, which squeezes free cash flow; AMD overtook Intel in data-center segment revenue in Q1 2026, at $5.8B versus $5.1B. Reported but not company-confirmed: yields on the 18A process may not reach profitable levels until late 2026 or 2027, later than investors had modeled — much of the 2026 rally rested on 18A ramping quickly, so a slip there undercuts the narrative directly. Separately, shareholder dilution from equity issuance around a $95 offer price is cited as a pressure on the stock. The counter-case is substantial: Intel and Nvidia have formalized a strategic partnership involving a $5B stock transaction, with analysts expecting the first integrated x86 RTX consumer chips around the 2026 holiday season and Intel-manufactured Nvidia components on 18A potentially by early 2027. That counter-case is named and cannot be settled here, because it depends on the same 18A yield question that is the source of the doubt. With disclosed foundry losses and rising capex on one side and an unverified process-yield timeline on the other, this suggests standing aside.
invalidation: An Intel disclosure confirming 18A yields at production-profitable levels, or conversely a further foundry loss expansion or capex increase without a corresponding yield milestone.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -20.8%. Corning reported Q2 2026 on 2026-07-28 with sales of $4.74B, up 17% year over year, and EPS of $0.78, up 30% year over year and ahead of a $0.75 estimate. Optical Communications, the AI-driven segment, grew 32% year over year to $2.07B. The stock nonetheless fell more than 20% in a single session because third-quarter guidance came in slightly below elevated consensus. Basis caveat: no source read this run labelled the $0.78 as GAAP or as Corning's core measure, so the basis of that figure is unconfirmed and is not characterised here beyond what the sources stated. The read is genuinely offsetting rather than directional. In favour: the quarter beat on both lines and the optical segment is still compounding above 30%. Against: optical growth decelerated from 36% in the prior quarter, smartphone demand for Gorilla Glass is described as softening, and the guide came in light — and on top of that, broader AI-sector rotation and profit-taking near all-time highs are cited as additional pressure, which is a market-wide cause rather than anything Corning disclosed. Nothing disclosed points to a deteriorating business, which is why this stays a long rather than an avoid, but a beat paired with a light guide and a decelerating growth segment is not a resolved read.
invalidation: Optical Communications growth decelerating below roughly 20% year over year, or a Q3 print landing at or below the guidance that already disappointed.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move +20.5%. Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 in late August; sources read this run state that adjusted earnings and revenue roughly doubled year over year and beat estimates, with fiscal Q1 guidance topping expectations, driving an 8.1% premarket move and a further extension to nearly 14% after the report. The stock ran from roughly $685 in early August to the mid-$900s by 2026-08-26. Multiple banks — Mizuho, JPMorgan, Raymond James, Citi and BNP Paribas — raised price targets citing datacom component demand, supply constraints and AI optical networking, with Raymond James flagging gross margins above 50%. The counter-case worth naming is that the whole optical complex de-rated over this window on a rotation out of optics and into memory, which hit COHR, AAOI and GLW hard; what separates Lumentum is that its own forward guidance moved up during that same window, so the company's committed numbers went one way while the sector narrative went the other. Verification limit, and the reason this is not rated higher: the sources read this run describe the beat qualitatively and give the pre-print consensus (about $989.9M revenue and about $2.98 non-GAAP EPS) but do not state Lumentum's actual reported revenue or EPS, so the size of the beat is unconfirmed and no reported figure is asserted here. The direction of the print is established; its magnitude is not.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 results landing below the guidance that drove this move, or a datacom order pause from a major customer reversing the supply-constrained backdrop.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -16.0%; the stock is down roughly 36% over three months. Coherent reported fiscal Q4 and full-year 2026 with Q4 sales of $2,045.5M and full-year sales of $7,118.2M, a return to profitability, Q4 EPS of $1.74 against $1.62 consensus, and Q1 EPS guidance of $1.85-$2.05, with Q4 revenue up 34% year over year. In August 2026 it began sampling 300mm high-thermal-conductivity silicon carbide substrates to major AI semiconductor customers for datacenter thermal management, and management describes bookings extending into 2028 with no demand pushouts. So the disclosed operating picture improved while the stock fell by more than a third. The explanation offered by the sources is explicitly not fundamental: the decline is attributed to dilution and profit-taking, and a separate sharp drop on 2026-08-10 is attributed to an optics-versus-memory rotation debate circulating on social media. That framing is itself the reason for low conviction — a move explained as flow-driven rather than as disclosed deterioration is not evidence of anything. Worse, the dilution leg could not be verified: a dedicated search this run found no Coherent equity or convertible offering announced in 2026, so the dilution attribution is repeated by sources but unconfirmed, and no dilution_risk flag is raised on an unverified raise. The counter-case is engaged and cannot be settled: a 36% decline against improving disclosed results means something in the picture is incomplete.
invalidation: Confirmation of an equity or convertible issuance that explains the dilution attribution, or a Q1 print below the $1.85 low end of the company's own EPS guidance.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -14.5%. Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-06 with EPS of $0.06 against a $0.01 estimate. Sources read this run also report revenue up 42% year over year, full-year revenue guidance raised above $1.1B, more than $324M of orders from major hyperscalers, a multi-year DOCSIS 4.0 agreement with Mediacom, data center revenue more than doubling, and construction started on a nearly 400,000-square-foot, $300M expansion of the Pearland, Texas campus to ramp 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers. The stock is up roughly 217% year to date. Note that one source attributes the 42% revenue growth figure to Q1 2026 rather than Q2, so the period for that specific growth rate is not cleanly established and is not asserted here as a Q2 figure. The tension is that all of the disclosed news is positive while the 60-day tape is down 14.5%. The explanation available from this run's research is the same optics-versus-memory rotation that hit Coherent and the wider optical group in August — that is, a flow and sentiment cause rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration. Discounting a decline that way is exactly the kind of read that cannot be confirmed from what was found, so conviction stays low even though the disclosed order book, guidance raise and capacity expansion support owning the name.
invalidation: The raised full-year guidance above $1.1B being cut, hyperscaler order momentum stalling, or a delay to the Pearland capacity expansion.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -13.5%. AMD reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-04; its own investor-relations release states second quarter revenue of $11.5B, gross margin of 54%, operating income of $2.0B, net income of $2.3B and diluted EPS of $1.38. Basis caveat: the source read did not label those figures as GAAP or non-GAAP, and net income exceeding operating income suggests the two bases are mixed across the release, so no characterisation of the basis is asserted here. Separately AMD launched the Instinct MI400 Series GPU family, including MI455X for large-scale AI training and inference and MI430X for HPC and sovereign AI workloads — a disclosed product launch rather than a roadmap promise. The decline that produced this signal is explained by the sources as rotation: the semiconductor sector saw renewed volatility in late August 2026 with investors rotating away from high-growth chip names, and the selloff is described as trimming gains rather than erasing them, leaving AMD below its recent high but still strong year to date. That is a sentiment and flow explanation rather than a disclosed deterioration, which is what caps conviction here — the pullback carries no fundamental information that this run could find. The disclosed quarter and the MI400 launch support owning it; the reason it is 18% off its high does not.
invalidation: A quarter showing data center revenue decelerating or gross margin falling below the 54% level just reported, or evidence that MI400 series deployments are slipping at named customers.

thesis: Signal: volume spike 2.17x against the prior 30 bars; the 60-day move of +9.4% did not clear the threshold, so this is a volume signal rather than a price signal. Sources read this run attribute the move to a 165 MW data center announcement in Finland, the launch of the CS-4 AI accelerator, raised guidance following a strong Q2 print, and sustained institutional buying. Two things are deliberately not asserted here. First, the Q2 print is described by the source as strong and as having led to raised guidance, but no revenue, margin or earnings figure from that quarter was found in any source read this run, so it is not called a beat and no number is supplied. Second, analyst positioning is not evidence: ten analysts rate the stock a buy and Morgan Stanley raised its price target expecting core revenue to more than triple by 2027, but that is opinion, not disclosure. The counter-case comes from the same Morgan Stanley note that raised the target: it warns about execution risk on more than 600MW of announced data center capacity. That is the central unresolved question — the Finland announcement and the CS-4 launch are announcements of intent and capability, and the distance between announced megawatts and delivered revenue is precisely what this run cannot settle. The counter-case is engaged and unanswered, which is what holds this at low.
invalidation: A disclosed slip in the Finland 165 MW timeline or in the broader 600MW+ buildout, or a quarter in which announced capacity fails to convert into the guided revenue.

thesis: Signal: 60-day move -10.3%. Marvell reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2026-08-27, and its own release gives both bases: record net revenue of $2.739B, up 37% year over year and $39.0M above the midpoint of the guidance issued on 2026-05-27; GAAP net income of $308.0M, or $0.33 per diluted share; non-GAAP net income of $865.9M, or $0.94 per diluted share. Data center revenue was $2.17B, 79% of total, up 46% year over year. The company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $12B from $11.5B, about 45% growth, and raised its fiscal 2028 outlook by $1.5B to $18B, about 50% growth. The tape did the opposite: the stock fell from about $241 on 2026-08-27 to about $211 by 2026-08-31, roughly 12% in three sessions, into a record quarter above guidance with both forward outlooks raised. A second, targeted search specifically to reconcile that decline returned no explanation — the sources covering the release contain no account of the stock's fall. That is unresolved evidence by definition, and per this pipeline's own rule a large adverse move that contradicts the disclosed facts means something is missing from the research rather than that the market is wrong. The disclosed results support owning the name; the fact that a record quarter and two raised outlooks were met with a 12% decline is the part this run could not explain, and it is the reason conviction is low rather than high.
invalidation: Finding the disclosure that explains the post-print decline — for example a guidance detail, customer program change or margin comment not captured here — or the fiscal 2027 $12B revenue outlook being cut.
